_comment: Secrets policy for the memory corpus. Enforced at INDEX time and again at,OUTPUT time (get / neighbors / search) — belt and braces, because an index,built by an older version of this server must not be able to leak.,NOTE: no plaintext credential appears in this file. Known literal secrets are,listed as sha256 hashes of their lowercased form (tokenHashesSha256) so the,denylist itself is safe to commit.,,Every pattern carries a `class` from the CLOSED vocabulary in lib/secrets.js,(credential-shaped / token-shaped / key-shaped; the hash route emits,known-credential). The marker is [REDACTED:<class>] so a reader knows WHY a,hole is in the text — and the class must never encode anything about the,redacted content itself: no lengths, no fragments, no charset hints.,The negative lookaheads match \[REDACTED[\]:] so neither the old bare,marker (still present in previously-scrubbed corpus text) nor the new,class-tagged one can re-fire a pattern. excludeFiles and sectionScrub ship EMPTY: they are per-machine. excludeFiles takes memory FILENAMES that must never be indexed; sectionScrub maps a filename to headings to strip. This file is public, so name files by path, not by what they contain.

patterns._note: A bare -p is NOT a password flag: unzip -p, mkdir -p and docker -p all use it. Scope the quoted--p rule to commands that actually take a password there, or the guard shreds the corpus.
patterns.name: cred-flag-p-quoted

patterns._note: 🟥 MEM-65. The quotes are CAPTURED and RE-EMITTED. This rule used to swallow both of them and put a bare marker where a string literal had been (`password: 'x'` -> `password: [REDACTED:credential-shaped]`), which is a SyntaxError in code and a mangled line in prose; test/public/campaign-lite.mjs shipped broken that way in two releases. Note also the negative lookaheads now sit AFTER the quote group, not before it: with them in front, a re-scan of the rule's OWN quoted output would see the quote, pass the marker check and re-fire.
patterns.name: password-colon

patterns._note: Same shape, same MEM-65 fix as password-colon above.
patterns.name: passwd-colon

patterns._note:
🚨 MEM-79. A password SAID IN A SENTENCE — 'My test password is Hunter2-Xk9!pass' — was stored verbatim: the two rules above know `password:` and `password=`, and the AWS key beside it in the same sentence WAS redacted, so the store file's description AND its search snippet carried the password in clear. This rule is the SENTENCE form, and it is deliberately narrow, because a rule that eats 'the password is required' is a rule someone turns off. Both halves must hold: (a) a trigger word — password/passwd/passphrase/passcode/pin — followed by a LINK (is | was | : | = | -> | set to | changed to, repeatable so 'password is set to X' works); and (b) a VALUE that is either QUOTED (any shape, 3+ chars — a quote is how a person says 'this is the value', which is why the plain word 'sunflower' redacts when quoted and not when bare) or UNQUOTED and 8+ chars carrying a non-letter, or UNQUOTED and 12+ chars. MUST STAY BELOW password-colon/passwd-colon: those two own the colon form, they run first, and their marker stops this rule re-firing — put this one above them and their own (a50)/(a92) fixtures stop proving anything about them.

THREE DETAILS EACH BOUGHT WITH A MEASURED FALSE POSITIVE over 2,956 real store files:
(1) the plain-word lookahead `(?!\*{0,2}[A-Za-z]{1,11}\*{0,2}…)` — Daniel measured 0 true / 3 false on bare lowercase words ('provided', 'supposed', 'extended'), and markdown emphasis must not smuggle one back in: '**provided**' is 12 characters with two symbols, so without the `\*{0,2}` it would satisfy BOTH shape rules. Bounded at 11 letters so a 12+ letter passphrase still redacts, which is the rule.
(2) the quoted branch needs WHITESPACE before the quote `(?<=\s)` — a trigger inside an inline code span ends with a backtick glued to the link (`` `Password:` ``, `` `password=` ``, `{pin:"exclusive"}`), and that closing backtick reads as an opening quote: 5 of the 9 false positives in the first measurement were exactly that shape, all of them documentation about this redactor.
(3) the gap may cross ONE newline but not a blank line — 'full password is\n<the password>' is a real leak in this store (the value on the next line), while 'the pin:\n\n`code`' is a label followed by a new block.
Daniel's rule as stated also wanted a LETTER in the 8+ case; his own fixture `PIN = 48213977` is all digits, so the requirement is 'a non-letter', which is the half that actually discriminates a secret from a word.

FOLLOW-UP — THE INDEX-STAGE BLOCKER. The first cut of this rule let a BACKSLASH be a value character and did not count one as a word terminator. In the SERIALIZED index — where the guard runs one last time over JSON.stringify(payload), stage `index-file` — a store exchange quoting this rule's OWN control case reads `must not redact \"password is required\"`, and `required\` is nine characters carrying a "non-letter": the rule fired, ate the escape, `\"` became `"`, the index no longer parsed, and buildIndex REFUSED TO WRITE IT. `npm run index` exited 1 and the staging index could never be rebuilt again. The 43 tests below were all green while that was true, because no fixture contained an escaped quote — hence the round-trip fixtures now in (a94). TWO NARROWINGS, both in this regex: (i) a value character may not be \ " ' ` , ; . ) } ] > or whitespace; (ii) the non-letter that QUALIFIES an unquoted 8+ token must be a digit or one of !@#$%^&*_+-=~?/| — never a backslash, a quote or a bracket. The plain-word terminator class gained \ } > as well. One consequence to know: in the serialized index a value written on the NEXT LINE is now left alone, because the gap wants a real newline and the serialized form carries the two characters \n. That is the right trade — per-field guarding has already redacted that text, this sweep is the last resort rather than the first, and a rule that corrupts the index is worse than a rule that misses one restatement of a value the field-level pass already removed.
patterns.name: password-in-prose

patterns._note: 🚨 MEM-64/MEM-65, the pattern that broke the shipped test suite. `['"`]?` consumed the OPENING quote of a string literal and `$1=[REDACTED:token-shaped]` never re-emitted it, so `const TOKEN = 'pubtok-...';` scrubbed to `const TOKEN=[REDACTED:token-shaped]';` — an unbalanced quote. test/public/run-public-tests.js shipped unparseable in the 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 portable zips; nobody saw it because the audit proves the secret is GONE, never that the file still parses. The quote is now captured as $3 and re-emitted (the CLOSING quote was never in the match — the value class excludes quotes — so re-emitting the opener is what restores the pair), and the separator is captured as $2 rather than normalised to `=`.
patterns.name: token-assignment
aws-access-key-id
patterns._note: Access key IDs only. AIDA/AROA/AGPA are IAM identifiers, not credentials, and redacting an identifier corrupts documentation for no security gain. The 40-char SECRET key has no prefix and cannot be matched without false positives, so it is deliberately not attempted.

The BODY is the secret; the header is only the label. This pattern used to be the BEGIN line alone, so a pasted key was 'redacted' into a marker followed by every byte of key material, which then reached the store, both indexes, get, get brief and a latest snippet (campaign B, B-1). Non-greedy [\s\S]*? so two blocks in one document do not merge into one match. This entry must stay ABOVE private-key-block-unterminated: the terminated form has to be consumed first, or the bounded fallback eats the header and leaves the body.
patterns.name: private-key-block

patterns._note: A truncated paste has no END line, and a block with no terminator must still lose its body. BOUNDED on purpose: at most 400 base64-ish lines, and NOT anchored on $ — an unbounded or $-anchored fallback would swallow the remainder of a whole serialized index at the index-file guard. The separator accepts a real newline and a JSON-escaped one, because the index-file guard sees the escaped form.
patterns.name: private-key-block-unterminated
